## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | confirmed |
| Confidence | high |
| Severity | high |
| Task Type | correctness / workflow safety regression |

### What Was Claimed

A bounded ForgeDock agent with `acceptanceRole: read-only` can successfully persist a trusted result without source edits, but pi-subagents subsequently reports a false no-edit implementation failure. The fix must reach the consumer path while preserving the no-edit guard for writers.

### What We Found

The bound integration revision has two role-definition paths. `src/agents/register.ts` registers the correctness and security reviewers as `acceptanceRole: read-only` but sets `completionGuard: true` for them; the implementation work-on role also sets it to true. `src/agents/materialize.ts` emits runtime agent manifests for the same roles, but `agentFile` hardcodes `completionGuard: true` regardless of `acceptanceRole`. `src/workflows/work-on.ts` calls `materializeForgeAgents` before spawning the bound child, so the generated manifest is on the provider execution path.

### Root Cause

The completion guard is not modeled as role-specific. Both the in-process registrations and generated manifests force the writer no-edit guard on read-only agents. A successful zero-diff read-only result is therefore treated as an incomplete implementation even after trusted Forge finalization.

### Affected Files

- `src/agents/register.ts` — role registrations must disable the guard for read-only reviewers and retain it for the writer.
- `src/agents/materialize.ts` — generated manifests must serialize the role-specific guard value instead of a constant.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — verified consumer of the materialization path; no behavioral edit is required unless tests expose an integration mismatch.

### Evidence

- The source registration contains `acceptanceRole: "read-only"` adjacent to `completionGuard: true` for both reviewer registrations.
- `agentFile` accepts `acceptanceRole` but emits the literal `completionGuard: true` for every generated agent.
- The work-on preparation path invokes `materializeForgeAgents(prepared.worktreePath)` before child spawn.
- LSP diagnostics are clean on the affected files before editing.

### History Findings

- Issue #49 tracks the earlier symptom and is closed with `workflow:merged`.
- PR #57 is merged, but its base branch is `dogfood`; issue #93 explicitly tracks the missing promotion to the shipping/consumer path.
- No decomposition is needed: the change is a bounded role-configuration fix with focused regression coverage.

### Recommendation

Introduce an explicit boolean completion-guard value in the shared materialization helper. Pass `false` for read-only reviewer manifests and registrations, and `true` for the implementation writer. Add a regression test that materialized read-only manifests contain `completionGuard: false` while the writer manifest contains `completionGuard: true`.

### Related Issues

- #49 — prior closed/merged symptom; not a duplicate because its fix landed only on `dogfood`.
- #57 — prior merged PR based on `dogfood`.

### Decomposition Assessment

Not required. The accepted scope is limited to the agent registration/materialization contract and regression coverage; no product, UX, security-authority, or protected-branch decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec

- Read-only reviewer registrations and generated manifests use `completionGuard: false`.
- The implementation/remediation writer registration and generated manifest retain `completionGuard: true`.
- A regression test proves the generated role-specific values.
- No unrelated workflow authority or merge behavior changes.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective
Make ForgeDock completion-guard behavior role-specific so read-only agents can complete valid zero-diff work while implementation/remediation writers remain edit-guarded.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/agents/register.ts`
- `src/agents/materialize.ts`
- `test/agents-materialize.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change `.forge/config.json`, state-branch data, leases, GitHub issue/PR metadata, merge/close behavior, or protected-branch policy.
- Do not weaken `completionGuard` for the implementation/remediation writer.
- Do not add a provider-specific bypass or special case for issue #93.
- Do not modify unrelated agent tools, capability ceilings, prompts, or workflow transitions.
- Do not include generated `.pi` runtime files in the commit.

### Invariants

1. Read-only registered reviewers use `completionGuard: false`.
2. The writer registration retains `completionGuard: true`.
3. Materialized read-only manifests serialize `completionGuard: false`.
4. The materialized writer manifest serializes `completionGuard: true`.
5. Registration and materialization use one explicit role-specific contract rather than relying on an implicit provider default.
6. Regression coverage proves the generated role values without requiring GitHub access.

### Deliverables

- Role-correct completion-guard values in `src/agents/register.ts`.
- Explicit completion-guard input and role-correct serialization in `src/agents/materialize.ts`.
- Focused materialization regression test.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check ID | Requirement | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AG-1 | Read-only agents complete zero-diff trusted work | Set false in read-only registrations and manifests. |
| AG-2 | Writers remain edit-guarded | Keep true in the writer registration and manifest. |
| AG-3 | Runtime contract is covered | Assert generated manifests for all three roles. |
| AG-4 | Scope stays bounded | Restrict the diff to the allowed paths and inspect with Forge Diff. |

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History

Issue #49 and merged PR #57 addressed the same symptom only on `dogfood`; issue #93 tracks the missing consumer-path promotion. The current staging base still hardcodes the guard for every role.

### Callers and Data Flow

`src/workflows/work-on.ts` prepares the isolated worktree, calls `materializeForgeAgents`, then spawns the child. The generated `.pi/agents/*.md` files and in-process `registerForgeAgents` definitions are therefore both part of the runtime contract.

### CI Surface

The trusted policy has an empty local verification-command allowlist. `forge_verify` therefore has no configured named checks; required GitHub CI is parent-owned after PR creation. LSP diagnostics and Forge Diff remain useful local evidence.

### Prior Findings

The investigation confirmed a false no-edit completion failure caused by `completionGuard: true` on read-only roles, not by Forge result persistence or issue routing.

### Hazards

The primary regression risk is accidentally disabling the writer guard or making registration and materialization disagree. Runtime generated files must remain ignored and uncommitted.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add an explicit `completionGuard` boolean to the `agentFile` input and serialize that value.
2. Pass `false` for correctness/security read-only manifests and `true` for the `forge-work-on` writer manifest.
3. Change read-only in-process registrations to `completionGuard: false`; leave the writer at `true`.
4. Add `test/agents-materialize.test.ts` to materialize the manifests in a temporary directory and assert read-only false/writer true.
5. Run LSP diagnostics, inspect the bounded diff, use the configured verification interface (which may report no local checks), then commit only the accepted files.

### Out of Scope

- Changes to pi-subagents provider internals.
- Changes to issue #93 text, labels, comments, or branch release policy.
- New workflow phases, retry behavior, reviewer policy, or merge authority.

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
